"modelAnswer": "Mountain ranges are linear or arc-shaped relief barriers whose alignment strongly controls local weather by intercepting winds and air masses. Major alignments include: Himalayas — east-west across Asia; Andes — north-south along western South America; Rockies — north-south/NW-SE in western North America; Alps — east-west arc in Europe; Urals — north-south in Russia; Western Ghats — north-south parallel to India’s west coast. Their weather impact is seen through five mechanisms. First, orographic rainfall: Western Ghats cause heavy rainfall on the Konkan-Malabar coast while creating a rain-shadow over interior Deccan. Second, climatic barrier effect: Himalayas block cold Central Asian winds and help maintain monsoonal rainfall over the Indo-Gangetic plain. Third, rain-shadow deserts: Andes block moisture, contributing to the aridity of the Atacama and Patagonia margins. Fourth, local warm winds: Rockies generate Chinook winds on eastern slopes, while Alps produce Foehn winds, raising temperature and aiding snowmelt/agriculture.
